papers.title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation
papers.problem: Robot arms fail when an AI agent hands them a task from a start position they cannot handle.
papers.fix: Training the robot arm on varied start poses widened its safe zone, reaching 98.4% success and cutting API cost 41.3%.
papers.practicalUseCase: If robots handle more start positions, agents hand over sooner and cheaper, so train robot skills on varied start poses.
papers.limitation: Results come from two simulated benchmarks, not from real-world robot tests.

papers.title: Reading, Not Adapting: Unlocking Frozen Visual Knowledge for AI-Generated Image Detection
papers.problem: Fake-image detectors that retrain big vision models often get worse on images from new generators.
papers.fix: A small add-on reads the frozen model's existing knowledge and reaches 91.2% average accuracy with only 3,074 trainable parameters.
papers.practicalUseCase: If frozen models already hold detection clues, you can skip costly retraining, so try reading them first.
papers.limitation: The 91.2% score is an average across eight benchmark groups, so single generators may score lower.

papers.title: OS-Omni: Benchmarking Generalist Computer-Using Agents on Long-Horizon Workflows Across Platforms
papers.problem: Computer-using AI agents get tested on one system at a time, not on long tasks across many.
papers.fix: The best agent scores 68.5% against 77.3% for humans, and trails humans by over 25 points on iOS.
papers.practicalUseCase: If agents lose track of state on long tasks, do not trust them with multi-step jobs on Apple systems yet.
papers.limitation: The result covers the first release of the benchmark, with 48 tasks per platform.

papers.title: DRBench Pro: A Knowledge-Centric Benchmark for Professional Deep Research Agents
papers.problem: Deep research agents had no test that checks which topics a report covers and how deeply.
papers.fix: Across 16 agents on 144 cases, the best agent reached only 57.04% overall coverage.
papers.practicalUseCase: If even the best agent misses about 43% of expected knowledge, check its reports against a second source.
papers.limitation: Questions and answer rubrics come from Wikipedia knowledge trees, so coverage means Wikipedia coverage.

papers.title: Islamic Social Financial Instruments and Sustainable Community Development: Evidence Synthesis on Community Resilience
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Research on Islamic social finance is scattered, so it is unclear which tool helps communities most.
papers.fix: In 93 studies, zakat gives quick crisis relief, waqf builds lasting assets, and sadaqah gives flexible emergency help.
papers.practicalUseCase: If the three tools do different jobs, combine them in one plan and back it with strong governance.
papers.limitation: This review only combines existing studies, so it adds no new field data.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Muslim-majority countries still exclude many people from banks, even though Islamic finance has grown fast.
papers.fix: Across 35 countries, income, schooling, institution quality and internet access shaped financial inclusion in OIC countries.
papers.practicalUseCase: If internet access and income drive inclusion in OIC countries, invest in digital infrastructure and youth and women first.
papers.limitation: The study covers only 35 countries and shows links, not proof of cause.

papers.title: Examining the Impact of Waqf Literacy on Waqf Behaviour
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Waqf collection stays low, and it is unclear whether public knowledge of waqf affects giving.
papers.fix: Among 642 Indonesian Muslims, more waqf knowledge improved attitude, social norms and control, which raised intent to give.
papers.practicalUseCase: If knowing waqf leads to giving, waqf groups should teach people how it works before asking for money.
papers.limitation: The data comes from Indonesia only, and the survey measures intent to give, not actual gifts.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Sustainability sukuk are growing, but nobody knew what decides how big each issue is.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk, equity-based contracts gave bigger issues, while paid second party opinions shrank them.
papers.practicalUseCase: If second party opinions cost money and shrink issues, issuers should weigh that cost against the benefit.
papers.limitation: Growth is concentrated in Indonesia, Malaysia and Saudi Arabia, so results may not fit other countries.

papers.title: From Clicks to Credit: AI-Measured Halal Product Awareness and Halal Financing Depth across OIC Countries
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: It was unclear whether online interest in halal products pushes up Islamic financing.
papers.fix: In 16 OIC countries, more halal searches raised Islamic financing, mainly through Murabaha and Ijarah.
papers.practicalUseCase: If halal search interest leads financing, banks should watch search trends and offer simple Murabaha and Ijarah products.
papers.limitation: The study uses search volume as a stand-in for awareness, and the effect on Mudarabah and Musharakah is weak.
